title: Domain Expert | CFO Office: Finance Process Mapping
description:
Description
About Factify

AI agents are starting to make decisions in regulated enterprises, including US banks and insurers. Factify turns an organization’s policies, documents and real-world practice into a sealed, executable rulebook that governs how those agents decide. Every decision is traceable, auditable and ratified by the people who own the process.
The role
You will be our finance expert. You will map how the finance function runs at large US-regulated enterprises, including approvals, controls, exceptions and close activities, and define the rules that let AI agents operate inside it without breaking controls.
What you’ll do

• Map core finance processes: record-to-report, procure-to-pay, order-to-cash, period close and consolidation, treasury, expense management and FP&A.

• Document approval matrices, delegation-of-authority rules, segregation-of-duties constraints and internal controls (SOX / ICFR).

• Analyze finance policies, accounting manuals and audit findings. Identify where documented policy and day-to-day practice differ.

• Define decision rules for tasks such as invoice matching, accrual and reconciliation thresholds, spend approvals and journal-entry validation.

• Build test cases and golden-label datasets with documented evidence, and review agent behavior against them.

• Partner with CFOs, controllers and internal audit to ratify the rulebook and keep it current.

Requirements

• 10+ years in finance leadership, controllership, finance transformation, internal audit or a Big 4 finance advisory practice.

• Hands-on US GAAP and SOX 404 / ICFR (COSO) experience at a US-listed company. This includes Israeli companies listed in the US.

• Experience with ERP-driven finance operations (SAP, Oracle, NetSuite or similar).

• Experience mapping and redesigning finance processes, with credibility with senior finance stakeholders.

• The ability to turn policy and judgment into explicit conditions, thresholds and exceptions.

• Fluent English, with clear written and verbal communication with CFOs, auditors and engineers.

• Location: Remote (US), with regular overlap with our Tel Aviv team (US Eastern morning hours).

Nice to have

• Experience with finance automation, shared services or an RPA / AI program in the finance function.

• CPA, CMA, CIA or equivalent credentials.

• IFRS exposure.

The role is full-time, remote initially until venture incorporation and spin-out (circa Q4 2027), location TBD.
The Problem Worth Solving
Across the UK, US and Europe, electricity transmission networks face an unprecedented construction challenge. Decarbonisation targets and the electrification of heat, transport, and industry require a dramatic expansion of high-voltage overhead lines - yet the construction methods used to build transmission towers have barely changed in half a century. Lattice steel towers are fabricated in large sections, transported by heavy goods vehicles and erected using mobile cranes that can cost £300K-£750K per project mobilisation. Foundations are over-designed because site-specific geotechnical data is too expensive to gather at scale.
Most cost-reduction efforts remain anchored in incremental optimisation: slightly lighter steelwork, marginally faster crane cycles. These leave the fundamental cost structure intact. Mass-dependent items - steel, concrete, transport, cranage and installation labour - still account for 35-45% of total line CAPEX. For transmission operators facing the scale of the UK's ASTI programme, or equivalent US and European grid expansion, incremental savings are not enough.
The Opportunity
We believe one of the most promising directions is fragmentation and modularity: decomposing transmission towers into standardised, factory-produced modules - small enough for conventional transport, light enough to assemble without heavy plant, designed for rapid field connection by semi-skilled labour. This approach has the potential to address not only the direct costs of tower erection and foundation installation, but the cascading cost drivers that inflate transmission project budgets: crane mobilisation, road upgrades for heavy transport, weather-dependent construction windows, skilled labour shortages and field operations risk premiums.
The commercial space remains wide open. Existing tower manufacturers and EPC contractors are optimised for the current paradigm and face strong institutional incentives to preserve it. Transmission owners are under acute regulatory and political pressure to build faster and cheaper but lack internal innovation capacity to drive a paradigm shift. The UK's ASTI programme alone requires £20B+ of new overhead line construction over the coming decade. Similar build-out pressures exist across the US and Europe.
Ultimately, the opportunity isn't to build a better transmission tower - it's to reinvent how transmission infrastructure gets built, so grids can expand an order of magnitude faster and at dramatically lower cost. Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

In this role, you would join Stripe's Vulnerability Management team, whose mission is to "Surface vulnerabilities at scale across Stripe." By joining our team, you will have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach, securely.

Our vision is to create a culture of continuous excellence in managing vulnerabilities. We want to enhance customer trust by giving users context about threats and vulnerabilities affecting Stripe's systems. We aim to be a key partner in Stripe's risk management by providing visibility into vulnerabilities across Stripe's products and services.

What you’ll do

You’ll build the systems that identify and prioritize vulnerabilities across Stripe’s codebases, production infrastructure, and employee laptops. These collect software bills of materials (SBOMs) across tens of millions of lines of code, scan hundreds of thousands of hosts for package and kernel versions, and connect that inventory to known vulnerabilities (CVEs).

You’ll also build agentic systems to investigate emerging threats. For example, parsing breaking security news, identifying the technologies involved, and determining whether Stripe is affected.

Alongside this engineering work, you’ll help teams across Stripe understand their exposure, prioritize fixes, and drive remediation. The role combines building data pipelines and security automation with hands-on vulnerability analysis and security guidance for partner teams.

Since our systems interact with the entire Stripe codebase, you'll work in Go, Java, Ruby, and Python. The services we own are written in Go, so most of your hands-on work will be in Go. • Continuously improve our security posture, processes, and tools

Who you are

• 5+ years of industry software engineering experience (does not include internships or co-ops)
